title: Compactability scoring and cross-shard fusion for paged-KV reclamation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a compactability scoring mechanism and cross-shard fusion pass to improve space efficiency and reuse of paged KV slots without compromising prefill/decode latency SLOs. The goal is to reduce long-tail memory fragmentation across KV shards, lower eviction-induced latency spikes, and increase decode hit-rate for multi-session workloads.
motivation: Existing paged KV allocation is suboptimal under mixed short/long context workloads. Fragmentation causes excessive background compaction, higher eviction churn, and decode penalties when a prefill must rehydrate widely scattered slots. Current heuristics (LRU window, age buckets) don't account for compactability or potential cross-shard adjacency. We need a scoring and fusion strategy to prefer allocations that are easier to compact and to opportunistically fuse nearby fragments across shards during low-util windows.
proposal: 1) Assign a compactability score to each allocation slot based on contiguous free-run potential, recent access pattern (prefill/co-access count), and model affinity. 2) Track a lightweight adjacency index per shard that identifies candidate neighbor slots across shard boundaries for fusion. 3) Implement a background fusion worker that, under CPU/GPU slack windows, migrates low-cost tokens into contiguous regions and updates KV mappings atomically. 4) Update the eviction policy to prefer reclaiming non-compactable slots and introduce an eviction hysteresis window to avoid oscillation. 5) Expose metrics and a runtime toggle in Console to observe compactability distribution and fusion rate.
tradeoffs: - Pros: reduces fragmentation, improves decode hit-rate, avoids frequent full-page compactions. - Cons: fusion/migration adds background IO and synchronization complexity; risk of increased tail latency if worker scheduling collides with decode prefill. Requires strong invariants to avoid model output regressions when KV mapping briefly changes during migration.

acceptance_criteria: 1) On benchmark mix (60% short, 40% long), fragmentation index reduces by >= 35% vs baseline. 2) Median and 95th percentile decode latency show no regression (>+5ms) after fusion enabled. 3) Eviction churn decreases by >= 20% measured as evictions/sec. 4) No correctness regressions in decode outputs across 1000 randomized prompt runs. 5) Metrics and runtime toggle available in Console; default off for existing clusters until manual enable.
